items.stem: Explain the term “tap root system”.
items.answer: A root system with a primary root and its lateral roots, as in mustard.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: a root system with a primary root and its lateral roots, as in mustard.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about the root, stem and leaf and their modifications is correct?
items.answer: In Australian Acacia the petiole expands, becomes green and synthesises food.
items.markingKey: (c) In Australian Acacia the petiole expands, becomes green and synthesises food. The other statements are false. Pneumatophores of Rhizophora help in getting oxygen; prop roots support banyan. Tendrils of pea are modified leaves; stem tendrils are seen in cucumber and grapes. Guava and Calotropis have opposite phyllotaxy; Alstonia has whorled.
options: Pneumatophores provide mechanical support to banyan.
Tendrils of pea are modified stems.
In Australian Acacia the petiole expands, becomes green and synthesises food.
Whorled phyllotaxy is seen in guava and Calotropis.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT a modified root?
items.answer: Colocasia
items.markingKey: (d) Colocasia is a modified underground stem, not a modified root.

items.stem: A plant part shows these features: help in getting oxygen; e.g. Rhizophora. Identify the modification. Give a reason.
items.answer: Pneumatophores
items.markingKey: 1 mark: pneumatophores; 1 mark: the features help in getting oxygen; e.g. Rhizophora are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Name the regions of the root tip and give the function of each.
items.answer: Root cap – protects the root apex; region of meristematic activity – cells divide repeatedly; region of elongation – cells elongate and enlarge, growth in length; region of maturation – cells differentiate, root hairs absorb water and minerals.
items.markingKey: ¾ mark each.

items.stem:
Vihaan grew a potato and a sweet potato in pots. Both produced swollen underground parts.
(i) Which of these is a modified stem and which a modified root? (1 mark)
(ii) Give one observable feature that shows the potato is a stem. (1 mark)
(iii) Name two other underground stems and state why they are modified. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Potato – stem; sweet potato – root. (ii) The potato has nodes (eyes) bearing buds. (iii) Ginger, turmeric, zaminkand, Colocasia; to store food and to act as organs of perennation in unfavourable conditions.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between pneumatophores and phylloclade on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A plant part shows these features: flattened green stem. Identify the modification – pneumatophores or phylloclade? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Pneumatophores: grow vertically upwards; help in getting oxygen; seen in swampy areas. Phylloclade: flattened green stem; leaves reduced to spines; carries out photosynthesis. (b) Phylloclade.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: phylloclade; 1 mark: “flattened green stem” is a feature of phylloclade.

items.stem: Which of the following is a modified underground stem?
items.answer: turmeric
items.markingKey: (d) Turmeric is a modified underground stem; the others are not.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between pneumatophores and tuber on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A plant part shows these features: bears eyes (nodes) with buds. Identify the modification – pneumatophores or tuber? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Pneumatophores: grow vertically upwards; help in getting oxygen; seen in swampy areas. Tuber: underground swollen tip of a stem; bears eyes (nodes) with buds; stores food. (b) Tuber.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: tuber; 1 mark: “bears eyes (nodes) with buds” is a feature of tuber.

items.stem: Which term describes the arrangement of veins and veinlets in the lamina of a leaf?
items.answer: venation

items.markingKey: 1 mark for the corrected statement, 1 mark for the reason: Guava and Calotropis have opposite phyllotaxy; Alstonia has whorled.

items.markingKey: ½ mark each: tendrils of pea – leaf modified into a tendril or spine; spines of cactus – leaf modified into a tendril or spine; stilt roots of maize – modified root; turnip – modified root.

items.stem: Define the term “aestivation”.
items.answer: The mode of arrangement of sepals or petals in a floral bud with respect to the other members of the same whorl.

items.stem:
Shreya cut a lemon transversely and found several chambers with seeds attached to a central axis. In a pea pod, she found seeds in two rows along one edge.
(i) Name the placentation in lemon. (1 mark)
(ii) Name the placentation in pea. (1 mark)
(iii) Explain one difference between them and give one more example of the first type. (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Axile. (ii) Marginal. (iii) Axile – multilocular ovary with ovules on a central axial placenta; marginal – one-chambered ovary with placenta as a ridge along the ventral suture. Example: china rose or tomato.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between marginal placentation and free central placentation on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) In the ovary of a flower: placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture. Identify the type of placentation – marginal placentation or free central placentation? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Marginal placentation: placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture; ovules borne on the ridge in two rows; ovary one-chambered. Free central placentation: ovules borne on a central axis; septa absent; e.g. Dianthus. (b) Marginal placentation.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: marginal placentation; 1 mark: “placenta forms a ridge along the ventral suture” is a feature of marginal placentation.

items.stem: Which of the following is a plant with free central placentation?
items.answer: Primrose
items.markingKey: (b) Primrose is a plant with free central placentation; the others are not.

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between axile placentation and parietal placentation on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) In the ovary of a flower: ovary is one-chambered but may become two-chambered by a false septum. Identify the type of placentation – axile placentation or parietal placentation? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) Axile placentation: placenta is axial; ovules attached to it in a multilocular ovary; e.g. china rose. Parietal placentation: ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or peripheral part; ovary is one-chambered but may become two-chambered by a false septum; e.g. mustard. (b) Parietal placentation.
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: parietal placentation; 1 mark: “ovary is one-chambered but may become two-chambered by a false septum” is a feature of parietal placentation.

items.stem: Describe the various types of aestivation and placentation found in flowers, with an example of each.
items.answer: Aestivation: valvate (Calotropis), twisted (china rose, lady's finger, cotton), imbricate (Cassia, gulmohur), vexillary/papilionaceous (pea, bean). Placentation: marginal (pea), axile (china rose, tomato, lemon), parietal (mustard, Argemone), free central (Dianthus, Primrose), basal (sunflower, marigold).
items.markingKey: 2 marks aestivation; 3 marks placentation.

items.stem: In the ovary of a flower: e.g. Argemone; ovary is one-chambered but may become two-chambered by a false septum; ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or peripheral part. Identify the type of placentation. Give a reason.
items.answer: Parietal placentation
items.markingKey: 1 mark: parietal placentation; 1 mark: the features e.g. Argemone; ovary is one-chambered but may become two-chambered by a false septum; ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or peripheral part are characteristic of it.

items.stem: Explain the term “pericarp”.
items.answer: The wall of the ovary that develops into the wall of the fruit.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: the wall of the ovary that develops into the wall of the fruit.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about fruits and seeds is correct?
items.answer: The plumule and radicle in monocots are enclosed in sheaths called coleoptile and coleorhiza respectively.

The plumule and radicle in monocots are enclosed in sheaths called coleoptile and coleorhiza respectively.

items.answer: bean

items.stem: A seed shows these features: hilum and micropyle visible on the seed coat; seed coat with testa and tegmen. Identify the type of seed. Give a reason.

items.stem: Describe the three layers of the pericarp of mango and state which layer is eaten.
items.answer: Epicarp – outer thin skin; mesocarp – fleshy and edible; endocarp – inner hard stony layer enclosing the seed. The edible part is the mesocarp.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each layer with the edible part.

items.stem:
Diya soaked a few gram seeds and a few maize grains overnight and split them open.
(i) In which seed did she find a large food-storing endosperm? (1 mark)
(ii) Where is the food stored in gram? (1 mark)
(iii) Name the sheaths that enclose the plumule and radicle in maize. Why is a maize grain called a fruit? (2 marks)
items.answer: (i) Maize. (ii) In the two fleshy cotyledons. (iii) Coleoptile (plumule) and coleorhiza (radicle); the seed coat is fused with the fruit wall (pericarp).

items.stem:
(a) Distinguish between a monocot seed (maize) and a dicot seed (bean) on any three points. (3 marks)
(b) A seed shows these features: two cotyledons, often fleshy with food. Identify the type of seed – a monocot seed (maize) or a dicot seed (bean)? Justify your answer. (2 marks)
items.answer: (a) A monocot seed (maize): seed coat membranous and fused with the fruit wall; single shield-shaped cotyledon (scutellum); bulky endosperm separated by an aleurone layer. A dicot seed (bean): seed coat with testa and tegmen; two cotyledons, often fleshy with food; embryo has radicle and plumule on an embryonal axis. (b) A dicot seed (bean).
items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a dicot seed (bean); 1 mark: “two cotyledons, often fleshy with food” is a feature of a dicot seed (bean).

items.answer: Castor seed is endospermic.

items.markingKey: (a) 1 mark for each of three paired differences. (b) 1 mark: a monocot seed (maize); 1 mark: “single shield-shaped cotyledon (scutellum)” is a feature of a monocot seed (maize).

items.stem: Give two differences between phylloclade and stolon.
items.answer: Phylloclade: carries out photosynthesis; leaves reduced to spines. Stolon: forms new plants at nodes; arches down to touch the ground.

items.stem: What is meant by “pneumatophores”?
items.answer: Roots that grow vertically upwards to get oxygen for respiration in plants of swampy areas such as Rhizophora.
